findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State how the effort builder selects anthropic_effort vs bedrock_additional_model_requests_fields (e.g. branch on the resolved id-shape: us./global. prefix => Bedrock key, bare claude-* => anthropic_effort), and thread any needed provider signal into build_model_settings/build_agent_kwargs.
evidence: Plan: 'send it through pydantic-ai 1.107.9's provider-scoped settings: anthropic_effort on direct Anthropic ... and bedrock_additional_model_requests_fields={...} on Bedrock'

structured_run.py:340-411 build_model_settings builds a single provider-agnostic model_settings dict with no provider branch; it receives `resolved` (model id) and `caps` but no provider signal is used for key selection today
The plan's own 'Ids and tables' enumerates bare (claude-opus-5-5) vs us./global. Bedrock profile ids, so provider IS inferable from id-shape — but the selection step is left implicit
findings.finding: The 'Effort, explicit' mechanism names two provider-scoped settings keys (anthropic_effort for direct Anthropic, bedrock_additional_model_requests_fields for Bedrock) but does not state how build_model_settings/build_agent_kwargs selects between them, since those builders currently assemble one provider-agnostic settings dict.
scenarios: Implementer sets anthropic_effort on a Bedrock request (or vice versa), so effort is silently dropped by the wrong adapter and the frontier/standard passes quietly run at medium instead of the pinned high

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State which model-id forms the new effort table keys on — enumerate bare, us.anthropic., and global.anthropic. 5.5 ids (as the capability-override table does) so the Bedrock-resolved us.* ids actually receive the pinned effort rather than silently falling back to the API default.
evidence: Plan: 'one per-model table beside the overrides pins high for Opus 5.5 and Sonnet 5.5' — no id-form enumeration
Plan 'Sampling.' section: 'Add each 5.5 id (bare, us., global.) to _MODEL_ID_CAPABILITY_OVERRIDES'
capabilities.py:223-253 (verified): temperature overrides carry separate bare, us.anthropic., and global.anthropic. rows per id because Bedrock resolves the us.* id form
Bedrock ids per plan: us.anthropic.claude-opus-5-5 etc. — the bare claude-opus-5-5 would not match a bare-only table on the Bedrock path
findings.finding: The new per-model effort table's key vocabulary is under-specified for the Bedrock id forms: unlike the sibling capability-override table (which enumerates bare + us. + global. ids because 'Regional and global Bedrock ids require separate entries'), the effort table is described only as pinning 'Opus 5.5 and Sonnet 5.5' / 'Haiku 5.5' with no statement of which id forms it keys on.
findings.location: Approach → 'Effort, explicit.' (per-model effort table); contrast with 'Sampling.' override table keyed bare/us./global.
scenarios: A Bedrock 5.5 run: the model id resolved is us.anthropic.claude-opus-5-5; a bare-keyed effort table yields no match, so no effort is sent and Opus runs at its default medium instead of the pinned high.
findings.suggested_fix: Key the effort table by the same three id forms as _MODEL_ID_CAPABILITY_OVERRIDES: map claude-opus-5-5 / us.anthropic.claude-opus-5-5 / global.anthropic.claude-opus-5-5 → high (same for sonnet), and the three haiku-5-5 forms → medium; add an edge test asserting a Bedrock us.* 5.5 request carries output_config.effort with the pinned value.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the rollback for the default-model cutover (e.g. revert the id constants to the retained 4.x rows) and its trigger (e.g. 5.5 provider-parity invalid:true or a failing post-change live run).
evidence: 'Replace 4.x ids with the 5.5 ids verbatim ... They go in the three toml files, config.DEFAULT_MODEL/VERIFIER_DEFAULT_MODEL ... DEFAULT_BEDROCK_MODEL_ID and provider_parity.CLASS_SLOTS'
'The per-model tables are ADDITIVE, so an explicitly configured 4.x model keeps working' — covers configured callers but not the flipped defaults
ABSENCE: no stated back-out mechanism for the default flip if the post-change live run or production surfaces a 5.5 regression
findings.finding: The plan flips the DEFAULT model constants (DEFAULT_MODEL, VERIFIER_DEFAULT_MODEL, TRIVIAL_DEFAULT_MODEL, DEFAULT_BEDROCK_MODEL_ID, CLASS_SLOTS) to 5.5 ids but states no explicit rollback/back-out path if 5.5 regresses in production. The additive-tables design preserves explicitly-configured 4.x callers, but the default path cuts over.
scenarios: 5.5 provider-parity run or a downstream pass regresses after cutover and an operator needs to revert defaults quickly
findings.suggested_fix: Add one line to Approach/AC: back-out is reverting DEFAULT_MODEL/VERIFIER_DEFAULT_MODEL/TRIVIAL_DEFAULT_MODEL/DEFAULT_BEDROCK_MODEL_ID/CLASS_SLOTS to the 4.x ids (rows kept by the additive design), triggered if the 5.5 parity run reports invalid:true.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a spike step that sends `effort` through the actual pydantic-ai 1.107.9 path (anthropic_effort on direct, bedrock_additional_model_requests_fields on Bedrock) and captures the emitted wire payload, confirming `output_config.effort` reaches the provider — not only the raw-transport probe.
evidence: Plan: 'probed on 2026-11-09 with one short call per case on each 5.5 model, on Bedrock (boto3 converse) and direct Anthropic (SDK)'
Plan asserts pydantic-ai 'copies into output_config.effort unconditionally (pydantic_ai/models/anthropic.py:1960-1978)' and merges at bedrock.py:706 — a version-specific third-party internal
Partially-verified: resolve_symbol UNRESOLVED for anthropic_effort and bedrock_additional_model_requests_fields; site-packages unreadable by file tools (not proof of non-existence)
No match in src/rebar/llm for anthropic_effort / bedrock_additional_model_requests_fields / output_config-effort — this is a genuinely new call surface
findings.finding: The wire probe (2026-11-09) that the plan relies on as its riskiest-assumption spike exercised the RAW transports (boto3 `converse`, Anthropic SDK), not the pydantic-ai 1.107.9 path the change actually ships through; so the provider's acceptance of `effort` is verified but pydantic-ai's TRANSLATION of `anthropic_effort`/`bedrock_additional_model_requests_fields` into `output_config.effort` is not exercised end-to-end.
scenarios: pydantic-ai 1.107.9 silently drops or renames the provider-scoped effort key, so no effort reaches the wire and Opus 5.5 runs at `medium` instead of the intended `high`
the Bedrock merge path emits a shape the provider rejects, 400-ing live runs after ship
findings.suggested_fix: Extend Step 1 / Testing-Live to assert on the serialized request (e.g. via a captured httpx/boto request) that effort lands in output_config.effort when driven through build_model_settings/build_agent_kwargs, on both providers.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the disposition the `refusal` stop reason surfaces (retryable/transient vs fatal/permanent) and confirm it is classified consistently at the call sites the audit touches.
evidence: "Walk every model call site ... against the five changes plus the `refusal` stop reason, and record one row per check (site, finding, fix or \"not affected\")"
The plan treats `refusal` as an audited stop-reason but states no disposition word for it; the audit output is 'finding, fix or not affected' with no required disposition classification.
findings.finding: The audit adds the `refusal` stop reason as a per-call-site check (a new failure-path consideration introduced by 5.5), but the plan never states its disposition contract: what the caller surfaces when a 5.5 model returns stop_reason=refusal — retryable/transient vs fatal/permanent.
findings.location: Approach → Audit: "against the five changes plus the `refusal` stop reason"
scenarios: A 5.5 model returns stop_reason=refusal mid-run; without a stated disposition the audit may map it to a non-retryable exception that masks what should surface, or leave it unhandled and surface a confusing generic failure.
findings.suggested_fix: Add one line to the Audit paragraph: e.g. "a 5.5 `refusal` stop reason surfaces as a fatal/permanent (non-retryable) classification via classify_llm_failure, distinct from a retryable Bedrock throttle" — and require the audit row for refusal to record that disposition explicitly.

structured.py comment: 'Measured botocore 1.43.64 supports it and 1.40.61 does not' — an environment precondition exists for the adjacent outputConfig surface

scenarios: an environment with an older botocore accepts the additionalModelRequestFields passthrough but the provider ignores or rejects the unknown output_config block
